summary: Closure run for TASK-006 - records the already-completed candidate and carries it into verification. The work was done by two bounded dispatches under the previous run RUN-b993e0a8bf114540b928219a986f65a7 (user decision route_5th = A: two bounded dispatches inside the same task, no new task ID, no clock or budget reset). Candidate: src/stores/queueStore.ts, sha256=0a88a6735c27b2fc2452fc02cc62af0234b8a0e7be4e1882c9bd8ea0e484feb6, 449 lines (was 256). PART 1 REQ-001 (worker 2c4ee3dc): the unreachable recovery branch in onRehydrateStorage was removed - it filtered status === 'running' while partialize never persists 'running', so it could never fire and persisted queued jobs were never handled; recovery now targets exactly status === 'queued' via isRecoverableJob, making persisted intent and recovery logic agree so no dead branch remains; recovery is at the store layer inside onRehydrateStorage, clears each job's node data.queued through the existing updateNodeQueuedState, waits for canvas readiness (canvasStore._hasHydrated plus per-job node resolvability; 25ms poll, bounded 600ms deadline) and then calls pump(); crash-loop brakes are a one-shot recoveryStarted latch, no retry/re-enqueue on recovery, and terminal statuses no longer matching isRecoverableJob. The worker additionally hardened updateNodeQueuedState's two floating dynamic imports with .catch() so an unattended startup failure cannot become an unhandled rejection - accepted by the manager as consistent with requirement 7. PART 2 REQ-002 (worker 2b35bfad): a synchronous guard inside queueStore.enqueue (no await anywhere in the guard) keyed by nodeId and restricted to that node's ACTIVE jobs (queued || running), so historical jobs never block regenerate or retry; whole-batch atomicity uses a per-node batch chain {shapeKey, nextIndex} where the batchIndex===1 call registers nextIndex=2 and later calls are admitted only as continuations (shape key match AND batchIndex === nextIndex exactly, then nextIndex advances), so a genuine second click restarts at batchIndex===1, never matches the advanced nextIndex, and falls through to the active-job rejection; single-image clicks have no batchIndex and are rejected by the same rule. The guard does not reference paused at all (paused occurs only in the state field, its initializer, togglePaused and pump), which satisfies the gate-invisible paused-state constraint that five review rounds identified. retry() sets an origin flag around its existing enqueue call so retry-originated calls never continue or open a chain, since retry copies batchIndex/batchTotal and would otherwise be field-identical to a continuation; the decision still happens synchronously inside enqueue. useImageGeneratorExecution.ts was deliberately NOT modified (no entry-level guard), matching the required store-layer placement. enqueue keeps its declared string return type and now yields '' on rejection; no caller consumes the value.
